title: Four jobs, four tools
scenario:
You run operations for an 8-person marketing team at a travel company. The team has paid seats on one AI chat product, and IT has one developer who can help. Your manager lists four jobs and asks which tool each one needs.

Use the exhibit. The company, jobs and notes are made up for this case. Product facts are from the vendors' help pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
JOBS (made up)

  A. Every Friday, 3 people write a client report.
     Same template, same 12-page brand guide, same
     client notes each week.
  B. Once a quarter: read 30 survey exports and build
     one spreadsheet with a tab per region.
  C. Tag every new booking request in the booking
     system as it arrives, day and night.
  D. Ad hoc: "make this email to a client shorter."

NOTES
  - Today people paste the brand guide into a new chat
    for every report.
  - Finance asks: "Job C is covered by our chat seats,
    right?"

questions.prompt: Job A: which tool fits the Friday report best?

options.text: A project that holds the template, brand guide and notes
options.explanation: Right. The ChatGPT docs say to create a project when work continues over time and depends on the same files. Each Friday starts a new chat inside it.

options.text: A fresh chat each week, with the brand guide pasted again
options.explanation: That is what the team does today. The same files come back every week, which is the case for a project.

options.text: An API link the developer builds into the reporting tool
options.explanation: People write this report themselves each week. The API is for software that calls the model, not for a team's own drafting.

options.text: A quick chat with no files, so the model writes from memory
options.explanation: Without the guide and notes, the model has none of the context the report depends on.

questions.prompt: Job B: what is the best way to handle the quarterly survey task?

options.text: Give it to the developer to rebuild as an API job each quarter
options.explanation: Nothing here must run inside another system. A desk agent can take the files and hand back the spreadsheet.

options.text: Hand the whole task to a desk agent and review the spreadsheet
options.explanation: Right. Many steps that end in a file is the desk agent job. OpenAI and Anthropic both say to check the result before you use it.

options.text: Ask one quick chat question and use the first answer as is
options.explanation: Thirty files and a spreadsheet are not a one-line question, and no vendor says to skip the check.

options.text: Make a project for it and type each of the 30 files in by hand
options.explanation: Typing 30 exports by hand defeats the point. The task has many steps and ends in a file: a desk agent job.

questions.prompt: Job C: who builds the booking-request tagger, and how?

options.text: A team member, with a shared project that staff paste requests into
options.explanation: Then a person must paste every request by hand, day and night. The job must run inside the booking system.

options.text: Each staff member, by asking their own chat to watch the inbox
options.explanation: A chat answers the person who opens it. Tagging inside another system with no one starting it is an API job.

options.text: The developer, who connects the booking system to the model's API
options.explanation: Right. Software calls the model through the API. The Claude Help Center calls the Console a platform for building applications and integrations.

options.text: Nobody yet, because AI tools can only be used by people in a chat
options.explanation: The API exists for exactly this: software that calls the model without the chat app.

questions.prompt: Finance asks if Job C is covered by the chat seats. What do you answer?

options.text: Yes. Chat seats include unlimited API use, so no new budget is needed at all
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center says the Claude API is billed separately. Max and Team plans add monthly API credits, which are a set amount, not unlimited use.

options.text: Yes, because the API is a feature that comes inside every paid chat seat
options.explanation: No page says that. The lesson's sources say API prices and billing are separate from the chat plans.

options.text: No. API use has its own bill. Budget it apart, even if a plan adds some API credit
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: the Claude API is billed separately, and some plans add a monthly API credit. OpenAI: API token prices are separate from subscription usage.

options.text: No, because the API only works for teams that have no chat seats of any kind
options.explanation: No page says that. The point is that the API has its own bill, not that it excludes chat seats.
